name: Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale
citation: Liebowitz, M. R. (1987). Social phobia. Modern Problems of Pharmacopsychiatry, 22, 141-173. Self-report validation: Fresco, D. M., Coles, M. E., Heimberg, R. G., Liebowitz, M. R., Hami, S., Stein, M. B., & Goetz, D. (2001). Psychological Medicine, 31, 1025-1035; Baker, S. L., Heinrichs, N., Kim, H.-J., & Hofmann, S. G. (2002). Behaviour Research and Therapy, 40, 701-715. Cutoffs: Rytwinski, N. K., Fresco, D. M., Heimberg, R. G., et al. (2009). Depression and Anxiety, 26, 34-38.
notes:
Liebowitz Social Anxiety Scale – self-report version (LSAS-SR; Liebowitz, 1987; Fresco et al., 2001).
Classic 24-item wording, as in the widely circulated self-report form. Copyright M. R. Liebowitz,
distributed by Mapi Research Trust (ePROVIDE) — check the terms for your use.
Each situation is rated for fear/anxiety and for avoidance, side by side as on the paper form.

elements.name: lsas_instructions
elements.html: This measure assesses the way that social phobia plays a role in your life across a variety of situations. Read each situation carefully and answer two questions about it; the first question asks how anxious or fearful you feel in the situation; the second question asks how often you avoid it. If you come across a situation that you ordinarily do not experience, we ask that you imagine “what if you were faced with that situation”, and then rate the degree to which you would fear this hypothetical situation and how often you would tend to avoid it (using the 0 to 3 scales below). Please base your ratings on the way that the situations have affected you in the last week.
